newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Bhutto protests at kidnap of politician.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Bhutto protests at kidnap of politician.

text.p: Pakistani opposition leader Benazir Bhutto on Saturday denounced the kidnapping of a politician in her Pakistan People's Party (PPP).
The PPP's deputy leader in the Sindh provincial assembly, Pir Mazharul Haq, was reported kidnapped on Thursday while he was driving towards the city of Hyderabad north of Karachi.
"It's a political kidnapping ... political terrorism," Bhutto told reporters in Karachi, the capital of Sindh province.
"We suspect Chief Minister Sindh, Liaquat Jatoi, (was) responsible for the incident," Bhutto said.
The Sindh provincial government has denied the charge, saying police are investigating the disappearance.
Bhutto said Jatoi came from the same district as Mazhar and had an old political enmity with him.
"It is not just Mazhar, who is like a brother to me, but all the leaders from the chief minister's district who are being victimised and put in jail," she said.

Bhutto, dismissed as prime minister by President Farooq Leghari in November on disputed charges of corruption and misrule, vowed to protest about the kidnapping to human rights groups and at international forums.
